_comment: ANNOTATED TEMPLATE — copy this, rename to <bot-id>-<scenario>.json, replace the values. The _comment* keys are ignored by the platform; strip them if you prefer a clean file. Shape taken from a real KKB Signals outbound call (see raya/testcases/args/README.md for how to read the real shape off a past call).
_comment_country_code: Always 91 for the India fleet. The platform prepends it to the 10-digit to_number you pass on the command line.
_comment_contact_phone: DO NOT SET THIS EXPECTING IT TO BE USED. ${contact_phone} binds to the number actually DIALLED (the tester DID), not to anything you put here. It already carries the country code — a prompt that writes 91${contact_phone} doubles it, which is a real bug class this repo checks for daily.
_comment_recommendations: The job inventory the bot is allowed to offer. This is the field that matters most: a bot given an empty or wrong-shaped recommendations list will either invent jobs or dead-end. A real reported 'bot is broken' turned out to be jobs sent in the wrong field, not a prompt bug — so always confirm the args before blaming the prompt. Keep job_id values EXACT; they are passed to apply_job and a stale id 404s.
_comment_contact_memory: What we already know about this caller from past calls. It is BACKGROUND CONTEXT ONLY — it is not a profile fetch, and the prompts forbid greeting by name or claiming the profile is ready based on it. For a genuinely-new-caller test use the literal string below so nothing is implied.
contact_memory: No Old Memory, Mandatory get_profile for the user
